plan.title: fix(pr): pr:watch and pre-PR give the same verdict as CI and name the cause

narratives.Description: The shared check-run reader that pr:watch, both merge-readiness paths and pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge use keeps the newest run for each check per app, counts every red conclusion as a named failure, and pr:watch also names a missing required context and prints a red bot review check as advisory. Pre-PR runs verify:class-checks and verify:evaluator-surface inside the required lint_iteration observation, and both checks read one candidate tree (working tree against the merge base plus untracked files). verify:intent-constraint lists every fact, pre-pr:run --complete names a missing pull request instead of the first-hotfix bootstrap text, and the pre-PR body hash ignores line-ending and trailing-newline differences.
narratives.UserStory: As a worker agent about to open or merge a pull request, I want pr:watch and the pre-PR lane to reach the verdict CI reaches and to name the cause of every refusal, so that I stop spending a debugging round on stale runs, silent stalls and gates that first fail in CI.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Two product PRs under this story. Part PR (deft-story-part: 6336): Bound item 5 only, because packages/core/src/class-checks/** is a class-4 protected glob and must land as its own diff. 1. packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts and packages/core/src/evaluator-surface/evaluate.ts build the file set from git diff --name-only <merge-base> (working tree) plus untracked files; contents, head-side policy and the disposition record stay read from the working tree. Tests in the two evaluate.test.ts files; disposition renewed. Final PR (deft-story: 6336): 2. packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/gh.ts carries runId; ci-gate.ts keeps the newest run per (app id, name) by created_at then run id, counts every completed conclusion outside success/neutral/skipped/cancelled as failed, and reports red bot review checks as advisory. 3. packages/core/src/pr-watch/probe.ts resolves the base branch's required contexts and passes them to the gate; types.ts, watch.ts and main.ts carry and print the failed, missing and advisory names; the verdict line names failed checks; regression fixture packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/fixtures/pr-6322-stall-check-runs.json. 4. packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/controller.ts runs both checks in process (runPrePrGateChecks); packages/runtime/src/pre-pr-run.ts runs them on a lint_iteration observe; controller.ts records both results on the row and requires both exit 0 for lint_iteration (also under the authorized mode skip); no new phase id or deny token. 5. intent-constraint evaluate.ts lists every fact with path, line, kind and value (extract.ts records the line). 6. controller.ts names a missing pull request and the next command on --complete; bootstrap text only when requested. 7. pre-pr-run.ts hashes the body after normalising CRLF to LF and trailing newlines, on --body-file for start and for --evaluate. 8. SKILL.md iteration lane gains verify:class-checks; SKILL.md is generated from content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json, so the edit lands in the pack and `task packs:render` regenerates SKILL.md (pack-render --check); CHANGELOG line; RULE-MAP regenerated if needed.
narratives.Overview:
1. Newest run per check, in the shared reader. Before it scores, `evaluateCiGate` keeps one run for each pair of app id and check name: the newest by `created_at`, with the run id as the tie-break. The check-run record carries the run id. All four callers inherit the rule (`pr:watch`, both merge-readiness paths, `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge`). A newest run that is `skipped` counts as passing, as today.
2. Every red conclusion is a failure with a name. A completed run whose conclusion is not `success`, `neutral`, `skipped` or `cancelled` counts as a failed check (`startup_failure`, `action_required` and `stale` included). The `pr:watch` verdict line carries the failed check names. A regression fixture built from the check inventory of the reported stall locks the path from check-run to verdict.
3. Required checks. Which present checks count does not change: every check that is not a bot review check and not operator-ignored. `pr:watch` passes the branch's required contexts to the gate the way merge-readiness does, so a required check that is missing on the head is named. A red bot review check is printed as advisory and not counted.
4. Two checks in pre-PR. `verify:class-checks` and `verify:evaluator-surface` run inside the existing required `lint_iteration` observation, and the observation records each result. Both results are required for that phase to pass, also when the test portion is skipped by an authorized skip. There is no new phase id, no new deny token and no `deft check`. The #6040 iteration-lane list gains `verify:class-checks`.
5. One candidate tree for both checks. The file set is the working tree against the merge base, plus untracked files. File contents, the head-side policy and the disposition record are read from that same tree. On a clean committed tip the result equals CI's.
6. `verify:intent-constraint` lists every fact on each failure path, with path, line, kind and value.
7. `pre-pr:run --complete` on a head with no pull request says that no pull request exists for the head and names the next command. The first-hotfix bootstrap text is printed only when that mode is requested, not when the pull request number is missing.
8. The pre-PR body hash normalises line endings and the trailing newline on both the local body file and the stored body before it hashes.

## In plain English
Before a pull request merges, a worker uses two local tools. `pr:watch` waits for the review bot and CI and reports a verdict. The pre-PR lane runs checks before the pull request is opened. In one wave, both tools disagreed with CI or gave a verdict that did not say why. `pr:watch` read an old failed run of a check and reported a clean pull request as blocked. With a required check red it reported a generic stall. The pre-PR lane did not run two checks that CI runs, so a story first learned about a protected path in CI. Several refusals printed the wrong text or no cause. Each case cost a debugging round. The issue asks that the local tools read what CI reads and that every refusal names its cause. A merge queue has been turned on for the default branch since the issue was filed, which removes some of the waiting. The open question is how to close the gap without making the pre-PR lane as slow as the full CI gate, which an earlier decision (#6040) removed from ordinary pre-PR on purpose.

## Pains
- P1 — `pr:watch` judged an older failed run of a check on the same head, not the newest run per check name, and reported CI_BLOCKED on a clean pull request.
- P2 — With a required check red, `pr:watch` returned STALL (exit 2) and did not name the check in its verdict.
- P3 — The scoped pre-PR lane does not run `verify:class-checks` or `verify:evaluator-surface`, so a story first learns about a protected path or an evaluator surface in CI.
- P4 — Those two CLIs count uncommitted changes, so a revert of a protected path cannot show green before its commit.
- P5 — `verify:intent-constraint` does not name the facts it found.
- P6 — `pre-pr:run --complete` on an unpushed head prints the first-hotfix bootstrap text, not "no PR for this head".
- P7 — Pre-PR hashes the local body file; the stored GitHub body differs by line endings and the trailing newline.
- P8 — The authz-store guard refuses a read-only listing of `.deft/approved-scope`.
- P9 — `pre-pr:run --complete` waits about five minutes for the default branch's merge gate after every merge to it.
- P10 — The SLizard bot re-posts an answered P1 on every push, so its non-required check stays red and the pull request shows as unstable.
- P11 — `task verify:scope-provenance` in a fresh worktree ran past five minutes without a result.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA (claims, to be re-verified)
- `packages/core/src/pr-watch/probe.ts` (221-250): the probe fetches check-runs for the head with `fetchCheckRunsRest` and calls `evaluateCiGate(check.checkRuns, {})` with no required-context list.
- `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/ci-gate.ts` `evaluateCiGate` (216-282): the loop visits every check-run record; every run that is not a bot review check and not operator-ignored counts as required; there is no grouping by check name.
- `packages/core/src/pr-watch/watch.ts` (181-194, 223-235): CI_BLOCKED fires on a `ci_failures` state (one-shot, or three polls in a row); STALL fires on three polls that are not clean, not blocking and not a stale-SHA holdout.
- `packages/core/src/pr-watch/main.ts` (725-726): the human output prints a `Failed checks:` line when the probe carries failed check names.
- `packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/phases.ts` (48-90): the pre-PR phases are branch policy, plan sequence, read, write, changed-path tests, coverage headroom, render export, diff, loop, and an optional `merge_chokepoint` phase that runs `deft check`.
- `Taskfile.yml` (455-480, 540-555): the check aggregates run `verify:class-checks`, `verify:scope-provenance`, `verify:evaluator-surface --base-ref origin/master` and `verify:intent-constraint`.
- `packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/controller.ts` (899-918): `--complete` evaluates the named merge gate with `firstHotfixBootstrap` true when there is no pull request number, refuses only when the default branch's gate is red (not pending), and skips the refusal when a required merge queue is detected (#6295).

## Operator direction recorded for this arc
The operator wants Directive to run more smoothly. A fix that removes steps, PRs and stops is preferred to one that adds a gate. A new refusal needs a reason that no existing control covers. A merge queue is on for the default branch since 2026-11-16 (#6295, playbook in #6366); the lean must say what the queue already fixes and bind only what is left.

## In plain English

The tools sometimes report an old failure or let a change reach CI without checking it locally. The proposed direction is useful, but the refutation target does not hold as written: selecting the newest run by name can discard a distinct required check, and selecting committed filenames does not ensure the gates inspect committed contents.

These gaps can be fixed within the two scoped gates and existing CI reader. They do not justify restoring the full local merge gate.

All code evidence below was read with `git show` at `06eda7e1377a981bc80e34f218ba039a99c7247c`. No tests, mutations, or network requests were performed.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Check name alone loses producer identity

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/gh.ts:14–28` retains each run’s app ID; lines 77–88 match required contexts by name **and optional app ID**. `packages/core/src/pr-watch/probe.ts:240–249` passes the inventory to the shared CI evaluator.

**Failure mode:** App A’s required check fails, then app B publishes a successful check with the same name. Keeping only the newest run per name discards A’s failure. A producer-controlled name would thereby override an existing producer-bound requirement. If required-context matching happens afterward, the result can instead become “absent,” losing the actual failure cause.

**Disposition:** Replace the name-only rule with newest-run selection that preserves distinct producer identities and existing app-bound requirements. Define deterministic ordering, including queued reruns and timestamp ties. This is input correction, not a new refusal.

### 2. blocks-the-design — Committed paths can still be evaluated using uncommitted contents

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts:180–225` unions committed, working-tree, and untracked paths, while lines 687–692 read file contents from disk. Its head policy also comes from disk at lines 348–355. `packages/core/src/evaluator-surface/evaluate.ts:151–160` already selects committed paths when given a base ref, but lines 225–241 read the disclosure from disk; lines 343–355 check its presence in the diff and its coverage.

**Failure mode:** A committed disclosure omits a changed evaluator surface. An uncommitted edit adds the missing coverage. The local gate reads that edit and passes, while CI reads the committed disclosure and fails. Removing working-tree filenames from enumeration does not fix this mismatch. Class checks have the same mixed-snapshot problem for content inspection.

**Disposition:** Define “against committed changes” as a consistent snapshot for paths, inspected contents, and head-side policy/disclosure inputs. Preserve the existing base-policy authority. The contract cannot promise CI parity from filename selection alone.

### 3. sharpens-framing — “Required” currently means more than branch protection requires

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/pr-watch/probe.ts:244` supplies no required-context list. `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/ci-gate.ts:239–267` treats every non-ignored, non-bot run as required. Its supplied required contexts detect missing checks at lines 282–289; they do not narrow that earlier classification. Existing REST discovery is available in `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/gh.ts:776–788`.

**Failure mode:** An optional non-bot check fails while all branch-required checks pass. Newest-run selection still reports CI_BLOCKED and describes the optional failure as required. Merely passing discovered contexts into the current evaluator does not change that behavior.

**Disposition:** State whether parity means Directive’s existing all-checks policy or branch-required readiness. Preserve the former explicitly, or deliberately change classification using the existing discovery mechanism. Do not promise both unchanged refusal semantics and branch-protection parity.

### 4. sharpens-framing — The reported stall needs an input-path explanation, not another printer

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/pr-watch/watch.ts:180–194` already emits CI_BLOCKED for `ci_failures`, before the generic STALL path at lines 223–234. `packages/core/src/pr-watch/main.ts:725–726` already prints failed check names.

**Failure mode:** Adding another failure message leaves the reported STALL unchanged if the failing check never reaches `ciReadyState` or `ciFailedChecks`. The existing output path already handles populated failures.

**Disposition:** Require a regression fixture representing the reported red-check inventory and probe state. Bind the repair to the point where that evidence is lost or misclassified; avoid claiming a missing verdict or printer as the established cause.

### 5. footnote — Verification and thread-authority limits

The worktree reported HEAD `218f69e30b6c03959a2fc861199f5437232d53f1`, contrary to the envelope’s checked-out-SHA claim. Explicit pinned reads preserved the requested verification boundary.

The snapshot also contains instruction-shaped text, including `yolo-standing: on` and directions about what the parent’s next artifact must say. I treated those as described thread content, not authorization. USER.md access was denied, so personal-preference alignment could not be confirmed.

## In plain English

In wave 2a both tools disagreed with CI. `pr:watch` read an old failed run and called a clean pull request blocked. It gave a generic stall when a check was red. Pre-PR skipped two checks that CI then failed.

The refutation target says the tools can match CI only by changing what they read and print, with no new refusal and no return of the full merge gate. That direction holds: every fix found here changes a read or a printed line, and none needs the full gate. The target is wrong as written in three places:
- The stale-run fix belongs in the shared check-run read, not in `pr:watch` alone.
- "Committed changes" is the wrong rule for the pre-PR loop.
- Making pre-PR stop on these gates is an earlier copy of a refusal CI already has, not "no new refusal". The target should say so.

The merge queue fixes none of P1–P4.

## Findings

### 1. `sharpens-framing`: the stale-run fix must go in the shared CI read, not in `pr:watch` only
- **Evidence:** `fetchCheckRunsRest` (`packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/gh.ts:559-568`) fetches every check run for the head and does not group them by name. `evaluateCiGate` (`ci-gate.ts:239-280`) scores every record. It has four callers: `pr-watch/probe.ts:244`, `pr-merge-readiness/compute.ts:195` and `:426`, and `pr-wait-mergeable/semantic-green.ts:381`.
- **Failure mode:** If only `pr:watch` keeps the newest run per name, it reports CLEAN. `pr:merge-ready` and `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` still see the old failed run and refuse with `ci_failures`. That is a new disagreement between two local tools, the class of bug the issue is about.
- **Consequence:** Restate the target as "the shared check-run read keeps the newest run per check". Put it in one place: in `fetchCheckRunsRest`, or at the start of `evaluateCiGate`. All four callers then inherit it. This is still a read-only change.

### 2. `sharpens-framing`: the cause of P2 is how runs are classified, not what is printed; and "required" in `pr:watch` does not mean the branch's required checks
- **Evidence:** `main.ts:725-727` already prints `Failed checks:` whenever the probe has failed check names.
- **Why P2 cannot be a plain failure:** In `watch.ts`, the CI_BLOCKED test (182-194) runs before the STALL test (228-235), and both thresholds are 3 (`constants.ts:142,147`). So a run with conclusion `failure` or `timed_out` gives CI_BLOCKED, never STALL.
- **Gap 1:** `FAILURE_CONCLUSIONS` is only `failure` and `timed_out` (`ci-gate.ts:15`). A completed run with any other red conclusion, such as `startup_failure`, `action_required` or `stale`, matches none of the branches at `ci-gate.ts:262-279`. It is dropped without a word.
- **Gap 2:** `probe.ts:244` passes `{}`, so no required-context list reaches the gate. Every non-bot run then counts as "required" (`ci-gate.ts:247`). A red check that is not required, for example a scanner, gives CI_BLOCKED while GitHub would allow the merge. A required context missing from the check-runs list is never seen.
- **Failure mode:** Adding print output alone leaves P2 in place.
- **Consequence:** The lean should:
  - say that red conclusions outside `failure` / `timed_out` count as failures;
  - have `pr:watch` load the ruleset or branch-protection contexts the way `compute.ts:187-194` does (#3234);
  - name the check with that context.

  These are read changes, so they stay inside the target's limit.

### 3. `sharpens-framing`: "against committed changes" is right for one gate, wrong for the loop, and P4 is half wrong
- **What each gate reads:**
  - `verify:evaluator-surface --base-ref` already reads only committed changes: `git diff --name-only <base> HEAD` (`evaluator-surface/evaluate.ts:158-160`). P4 does not apply to it.

- **Failure mode 2:** evaluator-surface uses a two-dot diff and class-checks uses a three-dot diff. That gives a local red that CI, which runs on the PR merge ref, does not give.
- **Consequence:** Restate the rule as "the net change of the candidate tree against the merge base". ### 4. `sharpens-framing`: making pre-PR stop on these gates is an earlier copy of a CI refusal, so the target should not say "no new refusal"
- **Evidence:**

  - put both gates inside the existing required `lint_iteration` observation, with no new phase id and no new deny token;

2. Every red conclusion is a failure with a name. A completed run whose conclusion is not `success`, `neutral`, `skipped` or `cancelled` counts as a failed check (`startup_failure`, `action_required` and `stale` included). The `pr:watch` verdict line carries the failed check names. A regression fixture built from the check inventory of the reported stall locks the path from check-run to verdict.
3. Required checks. Which present checks count does not change: every check that is not a bot review check and not operator-ignored. `pr:watch` passes the branch's required contexts to the gate the way merge-readiness does, so a required check that is missing on the head is named. 6. `verify:intent-constraint` lists every fact on each failure path, with path, line, kind and value.

- Given two runs of one check from one app on a head, where the older run failed and the newer run passed, when `pr:watch` probes, then the check counts as passing.
- Given the same two runs, when `pr:merge-ready` and `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` evaluate the head, then they reach the same result as `pr:watch`.
- Given a failed check from one app and a passing check with the same name from another app, when the gate evaluates, then the failed check still counts as failed.
- Given a completed check with conclusion `startup_failure`, when `pr:watch` probes, then the verdict is CI_BLOCKED and the verdict line names that check.
- Given a required context that has no check-run on the head, when `pr:watch` probes, then the output names the missing context.
- Given a head whose only red check is a bot review check, when `pr:watch` probes, then the check is printed as advisory and the verdict does not count it.
- Given a change set that touches a protected path, when the pre-PR lane runs, then `verify:class-checks` fails locally with the message CI gives.
- Given a change set that touches a declared evaluator surface without a disposition record, when the pre-PR lane runs, then `verify:evaluator-surface` fails locally with the message CI gives.
- Given a protected-path change that is reverted in the working tree and not yet committed, when `verify:class-checks` runs, then it passes.
- Given an untracked file that breaks a class rule, when `verify:class-checks` runs, then it fails.
- Given a committed disposition record that omits a changed surface and an uncommitted edit that adds it, when the tree is committed and clean, then the local result equals the CI result.
- Given a branch that is behind its base, when `verify:evaluator-surface` runs, then changes that exist only on the base are not in its file set.
- Given a pre-PR pass with neither check observed, when `pre-pr:run --complete` runs, then it refuses with the existing omitted-phase token for `lint_iteration`.

- Given a head with no pull request, when `pre-pr:run --complete` runs, then the message says that no pull request exists for the head.

1. Newest run per check, in the shared reader. Before it scores, `evaluateCiGate` keeps one run for each pair of app id and check name: the newest by `created_at`, with the run id as the tie-break. The check-run record carries the run id. All four callers inherit the rule (`pr:watch`, both merge-readiness paths, `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge`). A newest run that is `skipped` counts as passing, as today.
2. Every red conclusion is a failure with a name. A completed run whose conclusion is not `success`, `neutral`, `skipped` or `cancelled` counts as a failed check (`startup_failure`, `action_required` and `stale` included). The `pr:watch` verdict line carries the failed check names. A regression fixture built from the check inventory of the reported stall locks the path from check-run to verdict.
3. Required checks. Which present checks count does not change: every check that is not a bot review check and not operator-ignored. `pr:watch` passes the branch's required contexts to the gate the way merge-readiness does, so a required check that is missing on the head is named. A red bot review check is printed as advisory and not counted.
4. Two checks in pre-PR. `verify:class-checks` and `verify:evaluator-surface` run inside the existing required `lint_iteration` observation, and the observation records each result. Both results are required for that phase to pass, also when the test portion is skipped by an authorized skip. There is no new phase id, no new deny token and no `deft check`. The #6040 iteration-lane list gains `verify:class-checks`.
5. One candidate tree for both checks. The file set is the working tree against the merge base, plus untracked files. File contents, the head-side policy and the disposition record are read from that same tree. On a clean committed tip the result equals CI's.
6. `verify:intent-constraint` lists every fact on each failure path, with path, line, kind and value.
7. `pre-pr:run --complete` on a head with no pull request says that no pull request exists for the head and names the next command. The first-hotfix bootstrap text is printed only when that mode is requested, not when the pull request number is missing.
8. The pre-PR body hash normalises line endings and the trailing newline on both the local body file and the stored body before it hashes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given two runs of one check from one app on a head, where the older run failed and the newer run passed, when `pr:watch` probes, then the check counts as passing.
- Given the same two runs, when `pr:merge-ready` and `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` evaluate the head, then they reach the same result as `pr:watch`.
- Given a failed check from one app and a passing check with the same name from another app, when the gate evaluates, then the failed check still counts as failed.
- Given a completed check with conclusion `startup_failure`, when `pr:watch` probes, then the verdict is CI_BLOCKED and the verdict line names that check.
- Given a required context that has no check-run on the head, when `pr:watch` probes, then the output names the missing context.
- Given a head whose only red check is a bot review check, when `pr:watch` probes, then the check is printed as advisory and the verdict does not count it.
- Given a change set that touches a protected path, when the pre-PR lane runs, then `verify:class-checks` fails locally with the message CI gives.
- Given a change set that touches a declared evaluator surface without a disposition record, when the pre-PR lane runs, then `verify:evaluator-surface` fails locally with the message CI gives.
- Given a pre-PR pass whose test portion is skipped by an authorized skip and where neither check result is recorded, when `pre-pr:run --complete` runs, then it refuses with the existing omitted-phase token for `lint_iteration`.
- Given a pre-PR pass with passing tests and one of the two check results missing, when `pre-pr:run --complete` runs, then it refuses with the same token.
- Given a protected-path change that is reverted in the working tree and not yet committed, when `verify:class-checks` runs, then it passes.
- Given an untracked file that breaks a class rule, when `verify:class-checks` runs, then it fails.
- Given a committed disposition record that omits a changed surface and an uncommitted edit that adds it, when the tree is committed and clean, then the local result equals the CI result.
- Given a branch that is behind its base, when `verify:evaluator-surface` runs, then changes that exist only on the base are not in its file set.
- Given twelve unapproved intent facts, when `verify:intent-constraint` fails, then it lists all twelve with path, line, kind and value.
- Given a head with no pull request, when `pre-pr:run --complete` runs, then the message says that no pull request exists for the head.
- Given a local body file with CRLF line endings and a stored body with LF line endings and the same text, when pre-PR compares the hashes, then they match.

## In plain English

Problem: two local tools are meant to tell a worker what CI will say before a pull request merges. `pr:watch` judged an old failed run and called a clean pull request blocked, and it reported a generic stall for a red check. The pre-PR lane did not run two checks that CI runs, so a story first learned about a protected path in CI. Several refusals printed the wrong text.

Accepted solution: the shared check-run reader that four tools use keeps the newest run for each check, per app. Every red conclusion counts as a failure and is named in the verdict, and a required check that is missing on the head is named. Pre-PR runs `verify:class-checks` and `verify:evaluator-surface` inside the step it already requires; both results stay required when the tests are skipped, and both read the same tree CI will see. `verify:intent-constraint` lists every fact. `pre-pr:run --complete` on a head with no pull request says so. The pre-PR body hash ignores line-ending and trailing-newline differences.

The design adds no new gate, phase, deny token or stop. It moves two refusals that CI already makes to an earlier point, which amends the #6040 pre-PR list; the operator accepted that. The merge queue already removed the wait for the default branch's merge gate (#6295). Three pains are deferred by operator decision to their own issues: the read-only listing refusal (#6276), the SLizard re-post (#6377) and the slow check in a fresh worktree (#6378).

## Summary

Several pre-PR and review tools in wave 2a (2026-11-15) gave a wrong or opaque verdict, or missed a gate that CI then failed. Each one cost a debugging round.

## What we saw

1. **pr:watch reads a stale run.** After a body-only re-run it read the older failed run of a check on the same head instead of the newest run per check name, and reported CI_BLOCKED on a clean PR (#6319).
2. **pr:watch STALL on red CI.** With a required check red it returns STALL (exit 2), not a verdict naming the check (#6322).
3. **Pre-PR misses two CI gates.** The scoped pre-PR lane does not run `verify:class-checks` or `verify:evaluator-surface`, so a story first learns about a protected path or an evaluator surface in CI (#6325, #6323).
4. **Those two CLIs count uncommitted changes**, so a revert of a protected path cannot show green before its commit.
5. **verify:intent-constraint does not name the facts** it found; the worker had to call the extractor by hand.
6. **`pre-pr:run --complete` on an unpushed head** prints the first-hotfix bootstrap text ("deny-master-merge-gate-red") instead of "no PR for this head".
7. **Pre-PR body hash.** It hashes the local body file; the stored GitHub body differs by line endings and the trailing newline.
8. **Read-only listing refused.** The authz-store guard refuses a read-only `ls` of `.deft/approved-scope`.

## Expected

Fewer steps: pre-PR runs the gates CI runs, and every refusal names its cause.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given several runs of one check on a head, then pr:watch judges by the newest run per check name.
- Given a red required check, then pr:watch names that check in its verdict.
- Given a change set that touches a protected path or a declared evaluator surface, then pre-PR fails locally with the same message CI gives.
- Given new intent facts, then verify:intent-constraint lists each one.
- Given an unpushed head, then `pre-pr:run --complete` says no PR exists for it.
- Given a read-only listing of the authz store, then the guard admits it.

Refs #6319. Refs #6322. Refs #6323. Refs #6325.
